chunk_findings.detail: The new innocent-word handling deletes the matched text from the lower-cased string, which can concatenate the characters before and after the deleted word into a *new* agent literal. For example, with the production `words` set containing `claude`, the source line `x = "cldeclineaude"` has no `claude` substring, but `v.lower()` is `cldeclineaude`; `INNOCENT_WORDS.sub("", v.lower())` removes the embedded `decline` and yields `claude`, so `substring_sites` returns `[1]`. That is a false substring site introduced by the “fix”, and it can inflate the substring ratchet total or otherwise make the test report a wrong value.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_literals_substring.py:43 (`substring_sites` / `INNOCENT_WORDS.sub`)

chunk_findings.detail: `INNOCENT_WORDS = re.compile(r"decline[ds]?|declining")` is hardcoded to strip specifically the word "decline" and its inflections, but any other English word containing the agent fragment `cline` (such as "reclines", "reclining", "declination", "inclined", "disinclined") will still trigger a substring match and falsely count as an agent literal. Given input `x = "she reclined on the sofa"`, `substring_sites` returns `[1]` because `"reclined"` contains `"cline"` and is not stripped by `INNOCENT_WORDS`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_literals_substring.py:25

chunk_findings.detail: The innocent-word regex `decline[ds]?|declining` is greedy and non-overlapping, so it can consume the first character of a following innocent word. For `substring_sites('x = "declinedecline"\n', {"cline"}, set())`, the first match is `declined` (it takes the `d` from the second `decline`), the replacement leaves `ecline`, and `cline` is then found in `low`; the call returns `[1]`. That is a false substring site for a value that is just two innocent `decline` occurrences concatenated, even though the new `cldeclineaude` test only covers joining across a blanked word.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_literals_substring.py:43 (`substring_sites` / `INNOCENT_WORDS.sub`)

chunk_findings.detail: `INNOCENT_WORDS` is `decline[ds]?|declining` with no word boundary, and `[ds]?` is greedy. Blanking that match deletes the first letter of a following agent id that starts with `s` or `d`, so a real substring is no longer visible. Given `substring_sites('x = "declineswarm"\n', {"swarm"}, set())`, `v.lower()` is `declineswarm` (which contains `swarm`), but `sub(" ", ...)` consumes `declines` and leaves ` warm`, so the function returns `[]`. The same miss happens for `declinedevin` / `{"devin"}`. That breaks the comment on this line that the agent literal itself still counts; a ceiling ratchet then will not see the new site.

chunk_findings.detail: Replacing the innocent word with a single space still lets the surrounding text join into a multi-word agent literal. For example, `substring_sites('x = "clinedeclinecode"\n', {"cline code"}, set())` returns `[1]`: `v.lower()` is `clinedeclinecode`, `INNOCENT_WORDS.sub(" ", ...)` replaces the embedded `decline` with a space, producing `cline code`, so the `words` check reports a site even though the original string never contained `cline code`. The added `cldeclineaude` assertion only proves the old deletion cannot create a single-word literal; it does not prevent space-joined multi-word literals, which are in scope for agent literals such as `Claude Code`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_agent_literals_substring.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: `INNOCENT_WORDS` fails to strip inflections of "decline" other than `declines`, `declined`, and `declining` (such as plural possessives or third-person variations if any, or noun forms like `declination`), but more importantly, `cline` as a standalone embedded string or part of other common words like `reclines`, `reclining`, `inclined`, `disinclined`, `declination`, `microcline`, or `clinician` will still trigger substring matches for the agent ID `"cline"`. Given input `x = "she reclined on the sofa"\n`, `substring_sites(x, {"cline"}, set())` returns `[1]` because `"reclined"` contains `"cline"` and is not matched or blanked by `INNOCENT_WORDS`.
